words.explanation: n. [C] the land and buildings of a school, college, or university 校园
words.example: We have rooms for 900 students on campus.

words.explanation: v. to accidentally make a mark on sth., esp. one that cannot be removed, or to be marked in this way 染污；沾污；留下难以清除的污迹
words.example: The carpet was stained with red wine.

ad. used for showing that what you are saying is really true and not just an impressive way of describing sth. 确实地；真正地；不加夸张地
words.example: Now there are literally thousands of companies using our product.

words.explanation: a. relating to a suburb, or in a suburb 市郊的；郊区的
words.example: The suburban area has become one of the important tourist spots for vacation.

words.explanation: n. [C, U] ( fml. ) changing from one form or state to another 过渡；转变；变迁
words.example: China is a country in economic transition.

words.explanation: n. [usu. sing.] the type of person you are, including your character, your typical behavior, your abilities, etc. 自身；本身；自己；自我
words.example: Many people don't accept their true selves.

words.explanation: a. with a lot of details or small parts, which makes sth. difficult to understand or deal with 复杂的；错综的；难懂的
words.example: Few people understand the complex issues of economy.

words.explanation: a. new and never before used 全新的；崭新的；未用过的
words.example: I bought a brand-new bike yesterday. Would you like to have a try?

words.explanation: v. to feel as if you no longer belong or have a relationship with your feelings, family, society, etc.（使）脱离（关系）；（使）不联系
words.example: I took the train across the country and I was completely disconnected from my previous life.

words.explanation: n. [C] a word used in the names of some roads 大道（用于路名）
n. [C, U] 幼儿园；学前班
vt. to find a way to make ideas, beliefs, needs, etc. that are opposed to each other capable of existing together 调和；调解
words.example: The managers and staﬀ of the company are trying to reconcile their diﬀerences.

words.explanation: prep. used when comparing the advantages of two different things, ideas, etc. 与…相对；与…相比
words.example: The discussion is about the classic theme of love versus duty.

words.explanation: n. [C] a feeling that is hard to describe, caused by a particular event, experience, or memory 感受；感觉
words.example: Cathy often had the sensation that she was being watched.

words.explanation: vt. to make sb. leave their home for a new place, esp. when this is difficult or upsetting 使（某人）迁居他处
words.example: In 1954, my grandfather decided to uproot his family and move to China.

words.explanation: vi. to move or go somewhere without any plan or purpose（毫无计划或漫无目的地）漂泊
words.example: Many people will drift through life without any goals.

words.explanation: vt. to not have sth., or to not have enough of it 没有；缺乏
words.example: What shall we do if we lack hope?

words.explanation: a. steady and not likely to move or change 稳定的；安定的；不变的
words.example: The price of oil should remain stable for the rest of this year.

words.explanation: n. [C, usu. sing.] a position from which you can start to make progress and achieve your aims 稳固的基础；立足点
words.example: They managed to gain a foothold in the Chinese market.

words.explanation: v. to move quickly from one situation, position, or place to another, or to make sb. or sth. do this（使）快速变换位置
words.example: I can't bounce back and forth between my dream and real life.

words.explanation: v. to gradually get used to a new situation by making small changes to the way you do things 适应；使适合
words.example: It took her two years to adjust to life in South Africa.

words.explanation: n. [C, U] 1 a regular pattern of changes or events 有规律的模式；规则变化（模式）
words.example: I was adjusting to the rhythm of university life.

words.explanation: n. [C] ( fml. ) sth. that stays the same even though other things change 恒定的事物；不变的事物
words.example: His friendship is the one constant in her life.

words.explanation: a. ( ~ from ) clearly different or separate 明显不同的
words.example: The region's cultural identity is quite distinct from that of the rest of the country.

words.explanation: ad. in the beginning 最初；原先
words.example: Mary's family originally came from Germany.

words.explanation: a. 1 unusually good and special 极好的；难得的；不同寻常的；特别的
words.example: John has a unique talent for languages.

words.explanation: n. [U] the ability to make your own decisions without being influenced by anyone else 自立/自主能力
ad. 1 usually or most of the time 通常；大多数时候
words.example: The elderly generally get up early in the morning.

words.explanation: a. ( only before noun ) happening or achieving sth. at the end of a process 最终发生的；最后获得的
words.example: The price was what decided our eventual choice of the hotel.

words.explanation: vi. 1 to develop and become more successful 发展；成长；繁盛；兴旺
words.example: Their romance blossomed on a trip to China.

words.explanation: to happen in a particular way, or to have a particular result, esp. one that you did not expect 最后结果是；最终成为
words.example: It's hard to guess how things will turn out in the end.

words.explanation: to fall or go away gradually 逐渐坠落 ; 逐渐远去
words.example: Take a deep breath and let the pain drop away.

words.explanation: to be very easy to see or notice by looking or sounding different from other things or people 显眼；突出
words.example: Every tree, wall and fence stood out against white fields.

words.explanation: going in one direction and then in the opposite direction, and repeating this several times 来回地
words.example: The ball moves back and forth at the bottom of the screen.

words.explanation: to reduce the differences that separate two things or groups 缩短差距
words.example: We need a program to bridge the gap between the police and local young people.

words.explanation: to accept a bad situation or event and not feel upset or angry about it anymore 接受（不愉快的事）
words.example: It has taken him a long time to come to terms with his hearing loss.

words.explanation: every day for a long time 一天接一天地；日复一日地；天天
words.example: Dan studies day in and day out for the final exam, so I think he would get a good score.

words.explanation: to start living in a quiet and calm life in one place 安顿下来；安定下来
words.example: After years as a traveling journalist, she settled down in Ireland.
